newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Palestinians meet Israeli official on Jerusalem.
newsitem.headline: Palestinians meet Israeli official on Jerusalem.

text.p: Israel's Public Security Minister Avigdor Kahalani promised Palestinian officials on Tuesday to try to ease problems created by a closure in the West Bank and Gaza Strip.

Faisal al-Husseini, the PLO-appointed official in charge of East Jerusalem affairs, said Kahalani was the first cabinet minister to meet him since Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's right-wing government took office in June.
"Mr Kahalani promised to immediately find ways to resolve problems of Palestinians resulting from the closure which separates East Jerusalem from the rest of the West Bank," Husseini said.
A spokeswoman for Kahalani confirmed he promised to help solve problems related to the closure on Palestinians of the West Bank and Gaza Strip.
Israel sealed off Palestinian areas last February amid a series of suicide bombings by Moslem militants that killed scores of Israelis. It has at times been eased.

Palestinians said the closure was a violation of the PLO-Israel peace deal especially since it separated East Jerusalem from the rest of the West Bank and barred freedom of movement of people and goods into the holy city.
Israel declares all of Jerusalem its capital, but Palestinians regard East Jerusalem, occupied by Israel in the 1967 Middle East war and annexed, as capital of a future state.

The 1993 PLO-Israel peace deal stated that the sensitive issue of Jerusalem would be discussed in talks over the final status of the West Bank and Gaza Strip which have yet to resume under Netanyahu's Likud-led government.
"We also discussed Israeli confiscation of identification cards of Jerusalemites. Kahalani promised to arrange a meeting with Israel's interior minister to discuss the issue," Husseini said.

Husseini said Israel had rejected 2,000 applications for family reunification and had confiscated more than 200 identification cards of Jerusalem residents, effectively depriving them of any rights in the holy city.
"With such measures, Israel seeks to reduce the number of Palestinians living in the holy city," he said.
